records.Entity / project type: Decentralized P2P exchange software / coordination network
records.Concise description: Open-source P2P Bitcoin exchange network using local software, Tor and Bitcoin security deposits/multisig rather than a centralized custodial order book.
records.Deeper researched summary: Bisq coordinates fiat-for-bitcoin trades without a central exchange account. In Bisq v1, buyer and seller commit security deposits and trade bitcoin to a 2-of-2 multisig arrangement, with mediation/arbitration and delayed-payout mechanisms for disputes. Fiat payment occurs outside Bitcoin using the agreed payment method. A May 2026 Bisq v1 security incident affected altcoin trades and led to temporary hardening work; June 2026 project updates said victims were reimbursed and Bisq 1/2 development continued. This incident is important to current lifecycle/security context without implying fiat/BTC trades were affected in the same way.
records.Launch / history: Bisq launched in the mid-2010s (originally Bitsquare) and evolved into a Tor-based decentralized P2P exchange; Bisq 2 is a newer architecture alongside Bisq v1.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin exchange e: It is one of Bitcoin's longest-running attempts to coordinate fiat/BTC exchange without a centralized custodian or identity-gated account.
Important technical or cultural characte: Fiat settles outside Bitcoin between peers
2026 Bisq v1 security hardening is current context
records.Verification basis: Current Bisq project updates and documentation verify active development and the v1 multisig/security-deposit model; 2026 incident/reimbursement status was checked against first-party updates.
Research notes / uncertainties: Do not describe Bisq as eliminating counterparty/dispute risk; fiat settlement still depends on the peer/payment rail and dispute mechanisms.
The May 2026 incident and subsequent hardening should be rechecked before public security claims.
Bisq v1 and Bisq 2 are consolidated as one canonical Bisq entity unless Master Explore later needs implementation-level profiles.

records.Entity / project type: Federated Lightning P2P exchange coordinator network
records.Concise description: Privacy-focused P2P exchange system that uses Tor, Lightning hold invoices, fidelity bonds and coordinators to exchange bitcoin for fiat.
records.Deeper researched summary: RoboSats is built around Lightning rather than on-chain multisig escrow. Sellers lock a Lightning hold invoice and both sides post fidelity bonds; the chosen coordinator can settle or cancel the hold invoice and handles dispute outcomes. Current documentation explicitly notes that during payout the coordinator temporarily carries funds and that coordinator trust is not zero. A federation of coordinators reduces reliance on one operator but does not make individual coordinators incapable of theft or censorship.
records.Launch / history: Launched in 2022 as a Tor-first Lightning P2P exchange and later evolved toward a federation of independent coordinators.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin exchange e: It is an important Bitcoin-native design for small, private fiat/BTC trades that moves escrow logic onto Lightning hold invoices rather than a conventional custodial wallet.
Important technical or cultural characte: Coordinator can settle/cancel invoices and resolve disputes
Fiat payment remains peer-to-peer outside Lightning
records.Verification basis: Current RoboSats docs verify active service, Lightning hold-invoice escrow, fidelity bonds, Tor and the coordinator's actual powers.
Research notes / uncertainties: Do not call RoboSats fully trustless: the selected coordinator has material operational power during escrow/dispute handling.
Fiat payment risk remains between peers.
Use 'minimizes custody/trust requirements' rather than 'no custody anywhere'.

records.Concise description: P2P Bitcoin trading platform using 2-of-3 on-chain multisig escrow so the platform does not unilaterally control trade bitcoin.
records.Deeper researched summary: Hodl Hodl matches buyers and sellers while fiat moves directly between peers. For each trade, a P2SH 2-of-3 multisig escrow uses keys associated with seller, buyer and Hodl Hodl; two signatures are required, so the platform cannot move funds alone. User-side key generation and encrypted key material are part of its design. Disputes can involve the platform's third key, which means the service still has a meaningful coordination/arbitration role.
records.Launch / history: Launched in 2018 and has remained focused on P2P Bitcoin trading without a conventional custodial exchange wallet.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin exchange e: It is a durable example of on-chain multisig P2P escrow, contrasting with both custodial P2P marketplaces and Lightning hold-invoice systems.
Important technical or cultural characte: Seller, buyer and Hodl Hodl key roles
records.Verification basis: Current Hodl Hodl About/help and 2026 escrow documentation verify active service and the exact 2-of-3 multisig/key model.
Research notes / uncertainties: 'Non-custodial' does not mean Hodl Hodl has no role in disputes; its third key can participate in a 2-of-3 release.

records.Concise description: Mobile P2P Bitcoin marketplace using multisig escrow and a platform dispute role rather than a centralized custodial exchange wallet.
records.Deeper researched summary: Peach coordinates fiat-for-bitcoin trades through a mobile app. Current terms and support material describe a 2-of-2 multisig escrow involving the seller and Peach: neither can spend the escrow unilaterally during the ordinary trade flow, while timeout/dispute rules give Peach a defined intervention path. That differs from Hodl Hodl's 2-of-3 buyer/seller/platform design. Peach's 2026 legal posture around EU/EEA users is especially time-sensitive and should not be generalized from older availability pages.
records.Launch / history: Launched in the early 2020s as a mobile, privacy-focused P2P Bitcoin marketplace based in Switzerland.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin exchange e: It adds a distinct P2P escrow architecture and mobile-first experience to the Bitcoin exchange canon.
Important technical or cultural characte: 2-of-2 seller/Peach multisig escrow in current documentation
No normal centralized BTC trading balance
records.Verification basis: Current Peach terms/support material verifies active operation, multisig structure, dispute role and 2026 jurisdictional caution.
Research notes / uncertainties: EU/EEA availability/compliance posture changed in 2026; public copy must use a dated current source.
Do not describe the escrow as buyer/seller 2-of-2; current documentation gives Peach a key role.
